Echo, reverb (built or from a real room), chorus and saturation.

## audioDelay

Add an echo to an audio buffer

```js
audioDelay( audio, time=0.35, feedback=0.4, mix=0.35, pingPong=false, tail )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `time` | double | `0.35` | Seconds between repeats, 0.001 to 5. Use timeline.beat( 0.75 ) for a dotted eighth. Defaults to 0.35. |
| `feedback` | double | `0.4` | How much of each repeat comes back, 0 for a single echo up to 0.95. Defaults to 0.4. |
| `mix` | double | `0.35` | Dry/wet balance, 0 is only the input and 1 is only the echoes. Defaults to 0.35. |
| `pingPong` | boolean | `false` | Bounce the repeats between the left and right side. Needs stereo input. Defaults to false. |
| `tail` | double | optional | Seconds added at the end for the repeats to ring out. By default they run until 60 dB down, at most 10 seconds. |

**Returns** A new, longer audio buffer.

## audioReverb

Add reverb to an audio buffer

```js
audioReverb( audio, room=0.5, damp=0.5, mix=0.3, tail )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | A mono or stereo audio buffer. A stereo input gets a stereo-spread tail, mono stays mono. |
| `room` | double | `0.5` | The size of the room from 0 (small) to 1 (very large). Defaults to 0.5. |
| `damp` | double | `0.5` | High frequency absorption from 0 (bright) to 1 (dark and soft). Defaults to 0.5. |
| `mix` | double | `0.3` | Dry/wet balance, 0 is only the input and 1 is only the reverb. Defaults to 0.3. On sustained sounds a large room builds up level, so lower the mix for big rooms. |
| `tail` | double | optional | Seconds added at the end for the reverb to die away. By default it is picked from the room size, 0.5 to 6.5 seconds. |

**Returns** A new, longer audio buffer.

## audioConvolve

Plays a sound through the recorded echo of a real space: a church, a stairwell, a spring or a plate. The impulse response is a recording of a click or a sweep in that space, and the result sounds as if the sound was made there. Unlike audioReverb(), which builds a room from delay lines, this gives the sound of a particular place. <p> The impulse response can be any length up to 20 seconds and any sample rate (it is resampled). A mono sound with a stereo impulse becomes stereo. The response is scaled to unit energy, so level of the wet part is about the level of the input for noisy material.

```js
audioConvolve( audio, impulse, mix=0.3 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | A mono or stereo audio buffer. |
| `impulse` | any | required | The impulse response: an audio buffer from audioLoad(), mono or stereo. |
| `mix` | double | `0.3` | Dry/wet balance, 0 is only the input and 1 is only the room. Defaults to 0.3. |

**Returns** A new audio buffer as long as the sound plus the impulse response.

## audioChorus

Thicken and widen an audio buffer with a chorus

```js
audioChorus( audio, rate=0.8, depth=0.003, mix=0.5 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. On stereo input the two sides swing a quarter cycle apart for width. |
| `rate` | double | `0.8` | How fast the delay swings, in Hz, 0.01 to 20. Defaults to 0.8. |
| `depth` | double | `0.003` | How far the delay swings, in seconds, 0 to 0.01. Defaults to 0.003. |
| `mix` | double | `0.5` | Dry/wet balance, 0 is only the input. Defaults to 0.5. |

**Returns** A new audio buffer of the same length.

## audioSaturate

Round off peaks with a warm limiting curve

```js
audioSaturate( audio, drive=2.2, level=0.9 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. It is scaled to full scale first, so the result does not depend on its input level. |
| `drive` | double | `2.2` | How hard to push into the curve, above 0. About 2 is gentle and 5 is heavy. Defaults to 2.2. |
| `level` | double | `0.9` | The final peak level from 0 to 1. Defaults to 0.9. |

**Returns** A new audio buffer.
